question.problem:
The output voltage of a particular model of laptop AC adapters is $19$ volts on average. However, $1%$ of adapters have a voltage greater than $20$ volts. Assuming that the output voltage is normally distributed, find the percent of AC adapters with a voltage greater than $19.3$ volts, rounded to $1$ decimal place.

*Hint: A table of values of ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ for different values of $p$ is given below, where $p=Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $p$ | $\,0.900\,$ | $\,0.950\,$ | $\,0.975\,$ | $\,0.990\,$ | $\,0.995\,$ | $\,0.999\,$ | $\,0.9995\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${Φ}^{-1}(p)$ | $\,1.2816\,$ | $\,1.6449\,$ | $\,1.9600\,$ | $\,2.3263\,$ | $\,2.5758\,$ | $\,3.0902\,$ | $\,3.2905\,$ |

$$

$$

*In addition, you're given the following table of values for $p=Φ(z)$*.

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,0.6\,$ | $\,0.7257\,$ | $\,0.7291\,$ | $\,0.7324\,$ |
| $\,0.7\,$ | $\,0.7580\,$ | $\,0.7611\,$ | $\,0.7642\,$ |
| $\,0.8\,$ | $\,0.7881\,$ | $\,0.7910\,$ | $\,0.7939\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the output voltage of a randomly selected AC adapter. Then we have $X∼N(19,{\sigma }^{2}),$ and we want to find $P(X>19.3).$ But first, we need to find the standard deviation $\sigma .$ 

We know that $P(X>20)=0.01.$ First, we convert this to a cumulative probability:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 20) & =1-P(X>20) \\  & =1-0.01 \\  & =0.99\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we convert $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 20) & =0.99 \\ P(Z\le \frac{20-19}{\sigma }) & =0.99 \\ Φ(\frac{1}{\sigma }) & =0.99 \\ \frac{1}{\sigma } & ={Φ}^{-1}(0.99)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, 

$$
{Φ}^{-1}(0.99)≈2.3263.
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sigma } & =2.3263 \\ \sigma  & =\frac{1}{2.32639} \\  & ≈0.42985.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can solve for $P(X>19.3)$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>19.3) & =1-P(X\le 19.3) \\  & =1-P(Z\le \frac{19.3-19}{0.42985}) \\  & ≈1-P(Z\le 0.70) \\  & =1-Φ(0.70) \\  & =1-0.7580 \\  & ≈24.2%\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, approximately $24.2%$ of AC adapters have a voltage greater than $19.3$ volts.
